data.cultural_impact: The name "Sokeen" holds a rich cultural significance in Hindu tradition, derived from the Sanskrit term "Sooraj," meaning "Sun." This diminutive form of the name signifies a deep connection to the divine celestial body. In Hindu mythology, the sun is worshipped as a powerful deity, Surya, illuminating the world and symbolizing life, vitality, and the cycle of day and night. The name "Sokeen" may have originally been given to acknowledge and honor an individual born under the reign of the Sun or as a term of endearment meaning "little one," implying affection and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: The cultural background of the name "Sokeen," derived from the term "Sooraj," holds a profound spiritual significance as well. In Hindu spirituality, the sun signifies the divine force within us and represents knowledge, inner-light, and transformation. The name "Sokeen" may serve as a constant reminder for the bearer to seek knowledge and inner illumination, and to look within for self-realization and spiritual growth. The name's connection to the radiant Sun is a subtle influence encouraging individuals to radiate positivity, love, and light into the world.

historical_references.reference: The Sokas or Soces, a community of Jains in ancient India, are mentioned in the 5th-century-CE text 'Harivamsa', which is an appendix to the Indian epic 'Mahabharata'. The Sokas are described as devout followers of Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, and practitioners of strict asceticism.

According to the 'Bhavishy Purana' (13th-14th century CE), a Hindu prophetic text, a king named Soke Khan or Soke Singh ruled over the region of Kashmir. He was a great devotee of Lord Shiva and is known to have patronized the construction and renovation of various Shiva temples in the region during his reign.
historical_references.context: Ruler of Kashmir mentioned in 'Bhavishy Purana'
